passage:
The metro was almost empty at midnight, and Aparna was still smiling at the window. Tarun had walked her to the station after the department party, and at the platform he had kissed her. She'd let him. Her heart was racing with something bright and forbidden.

By the second station, the brightness had turned into a cold weight. Her phone buzzed: Akash, asking if she'd reached safely, telling her to sleep well. She read it three times.

She had told herself lately that Akash was too busy to notice her. That was true. It also wasn't a reason. She'd chosen this.

At home she blocked Tarun's number, then sat on the edge of her bed. Tomorrow she would ask Akash to meet, tell him plainly, and not blame him. Her stomach ached at the thought.

qa.a: He kissed her at the platform after the department party.

qa.q: What was Aparna feeling by the second station, and how does the passage show it?
qa.a: She felt dread and guilt, since the brightness turned into a cold weight, and she read Akash's message three times.

qa.q: What did Aparna do that ends the deception, and what will she face next?
qa.a: She blocked Tarun's number and planned to tell Akash plainly without blaming him; next she has to face how he reacts and accept the consequences.

qa.q: How might Akash feel if he hears about the kiss from Aparna herself instead of finding out elsewhere?
qa.a: He would probably be hurt and angry, but he may also see that she chose to be honest rather than hiding it.

grounding: Shows crossing a line with a thrill then guilt and dread, and a first step toward honest admission without blaming the partner.

passage:
Dear Nazia,
I'm writing because I owe you the truth in full, not in pieces.
At the conference in Hyderabad last month, I kissed someone. It happened on the last night. In the moment I felt a rush, as if I were someone new. By morning I felt sick, and I've felt sick every day since. I lied to you on the phone when you asked how the trip was. That was the second betrayal.
I've thought about why. It isn't because of anything you did. I've been feeling lost about my career, and I went looking for a thrill instead of talking to you. That's on me, completely.
I've ended all contact with her. I'm not asking you to forgive me, and I'm not asking you to decide anything soon. Whatever you choose, I'll accept it. If you want to talk, I'll be there. If you don't, I'll understand.
I'm so sorry.
Lokesh

qa.q: Where did Lokesh cross the line?
qa.a: At the conference in Hyderabad, on the last night.

qa.q: How did Lokesh feel the morning after?
qa.a: Lokesh felt sick with guilt, and has felt that dread every day since.

qa.q: What does Lokesh do right in this letter?
qa.a: Admits the full truth, owns the reason without blaming Nazia, ends contact, and accepts whatever Nazia decides.

qa.q: How might Nazia feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Likely hurt and shocked, but at least told the whole truth rather than lied to further.

grounding: A letter from a young person who cheated, feeling a thrill then guilt, admitting it fully, ending the deception and accepting the consequences without blame.

passage: Eshaan, you're the only one I can say this to. I'm Deepak, and I cheated on Kavya. There, it's out. It started as texting a girl from my gym. It felt exciting, like being in a film. Then we met twice. The first week I felt this buzz. The second week I couldn't sleep. When Kavya asked why I was always on my phone, I lied. When she pushed, I snapped: 'You're so busy with your MBA, what did you expect?' I actually said that. Blamed her for my choice. Then I went home and sat with it. It wasn't her MBA. It was me wanting to feel wanted without doing the work of telling her I felt ignored. So yesterday I told her everything. No excuses. I ended it with the girl from the gym. Kavya cried and asked me to leave. I want her to forgive me so badly. But I don't get to demand that. I just have to live with what I did, and be honest from here.

qa.q: Where did Deepak meet the girl he texted?
What did Deepak feel in the second week?
qa.a: He felt guilty and full of dread, unable to sleep after the first week's thrill.

qa.q: What did Deepak eventually do right?
qa.a: He told Kavya everything without excuses, ended the other relationship, and accepted that he can't demand forgiveness.

qa.q: How did Kavya respond when Deepak told her?
qa.a: She cried and asked him to leave.

grounding: A spoken account of a young man who cheated, first blaming his partner and lying, then confessing honestly, ending it and accepting the consequences.
